notable_claims: This is believed to be the first lawsuit filed by a student against an institution for denying computer network access.
The university's policy restricted campus computer use to activities directly related to educational purposes.
classification.summary: A graduate student at the University of Texas at Dallas filed a $2-million lawsuit after being barred from the campus network for posting political commentary on Russian and Ukrainian affairs. The university cited rules restricting computer use to educational purposes, while the student alleged First Amendment violations and censorship. This case is noted as potentially the first lawsuit of its kind regarding the balance between free speech and institutional control of computer resources.
classification.title: Free Speech vs. Computer Rules

notable_claims: The Ontario government's framework defines offensive or inappropriate comments as harassment without distinguishing protected speech.
The requirement for universities to submit policy reviews and annual reports to the government undermines institutional autonomy.
classification.summary: Carl M. Kadie critiques a 'Framework Regarding Prevention of Harassment and Discrimination in Ontario Universities,' arguing that its broad definition of harassment threatens academic freedom and institutional autonomy. The post includes the government's framework and a contrasting policy statement from the AAUP advocating against campus speech codes.
classification.title: Re: Government of Ontario university speech code

identity.subject: Re: Government of Ontario university speech code

notable_claims: The suit alleged copyright violations occurred at least 690 times.
The plaintiff sought $100,000 for each instance of infringement.
classification.summary: A lawsuit was filed against CompuServe alleging copyright infringement of the song 'Unchained Melody' via MIDI file uploads and downloads. The plaintiff sought to hold the service provider liable rather than individual users due to the impracticality of pursuing numerous individuals. This case highlights early legal efforts to establish intermediary liability for user-generated content on online services.
classification.title: New lawsuit: Is CompuServe liable for infringing uploads?

identity.subject: New lawsuit: Is CompuServe liable for infringing uploads?
